bullets: Stave 1: ‘cold, bleak, biting weather: foggy withal’; ‘the fog came pouring in at every chink and keyhole’: fog symbolises **moral blindness** and isolation.
‘Darkness is cheap, and Scrooge liked it’: his meanness extends to light; also suggests spiritual darkness.
Scrooge’s house is in a gloomy yard, ‘so dull’ that even Scrooge has to grope his way.
The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come is dark, shrouded and silent.
Ghost of Christmas Past: ‘from the crown of its head there sprung a bright clear jet of light’: truth, memory, revelation.
Scrooge pushes the extinguisher-cap down on it but cannot hide the light: truth cannot be suppressed.
Ghost of Christmas Present’s torch, like a horn of plenty, and the blazing fire.
Stave 5: ‘No fog, no mist; clear, bright, jovial, stirring, cold… Golden sunlight; Heavenly sky; sweet fresh air; merry bells.’
Cold and fog in Stave 1 = coldness and blindness.
Bright, clear sunshine in Stave 5 = joy, clarity, redemption.
Note: Stave 5 is still ‘cold’, but now ‘piping for the blood to dance to’: same weather, different perception.

callouts.p: Dickens uses light and weather to externalise Scrooge’s soul: darkness and fog reflect his moral blindness, while the light of the Ghosts and the golden Christmas morning reflect truth and redemption.

core.p: The weather reflects Scrooge’s inner state.

model: Warm interiors of the Cratchits and Fezziwig
exam.q: Explain how Dickens uses setting and weather elsewhere in the novella. (20 marks)
exam.tip: Contrast Stave 1 and Stave 5 weather directly.

mistakes.r: It is still cold, but described joyfully: perception has changed.
mistakes.w: Saying it is warm in Stave 5.

quotes.q: Darkness is cheap, and Scrooge liked it
the fog came pouring in at every chink and keyhole
a bright clear jet of light

summary: Light and dark and the weather are symbolic throughout: fog, darkness and cold surround Scrooge in Stave 1, the Ghosts bring light, and Stave 5 opens on a bright, clear, golden morning that reflects his inner change.

terms.d: Weather or nature reflecting human emotions.
Using an object or image to represent an idea.
